purpose: Improvement suggestions for the site and the underlying program, written so a reviewer can choose a path before anything is implemented. Nothing here is applied automatically: every row carries a decision to be made, the evidence behind it, the options considered and a recommendation. Status values are PROPOSED, RECOMMENDED, DEFERRED and REJECTED; only the reviewer changes a status.

suggestions.title: Schedule the existing official fetch workflow weekly (and before each week's first reporting day) so schedule changes like the Nov 9 Week 11 move are caught within days, not discovered later.
suggestions.problem: Prevents stale rows (IR-022 class) from reaching the leaderboard's grading substrate.
suggestions.evidence: NFL.com Week 11 schedule change (the missed-change example)
options: Review the linked official evidence and decide before implementation.
suggestions.recommendation: Proposed in the already merged NFL Lines module; this is not an approval to implement.
suggestions.decision_needed: Enable scheduled runs against main; add a diff report of changed official rows.

suggestions.title: Show a per-row last-verified age and a visible STALE badge when an official announcement post-dates a row's capture; link the correcting announcement on the row.
suggestions.problem: Line-origination decisions stop relying on silently outdated rows.
suggestions.evidence: NFL.com Week 11 schedule change
options: Review the linked official evidence and decide before implementation.
suggestions.recommendation: Proposed in the already merged NFL Lines module; this is not an approval to implement.
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve the badge design; decide whether stale rows stay visible with the badge or move to a quarantine table.

suggestions.title: Capture the official injury report every reporting day and render per-team availability deltas (DNP/Limited/Out counts + key absences) next to each game row on the daily scoreboard.
suggestions.problem: Makes the availability signal (G-01) usable for line origination without manual reading of 32 team tables.
suggestions.evidence: NFL.com injury report
options: Review the linked official evidence and decide before implementation.
suggestions.recommendation: Proposed in the already merged NFL Lines module; this is not an approval to implement.
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve weekly-capture storage layout and the delta display.

suggestions.title: Build a per-club depth-order collection from official club announcements/sites since NFL.com does not publish depth order (IR-023); start with FOCUS clubs, expand gradually.
suggestions.problem: Unlocks the starter-to-backup downgrade signal (G-02) and the deficiency metrics (D-01–D-03).
suggestions.evidence: NFL.com team depth-chart URL (404 evidence, IR-023)
options: Review the linked official evidence and decide before implementation.
suggestions.recommendation: Proposed in the already merged NFL Lines module; this is not an approval to implement.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm the depth-order authority per club and storage schema.

suggestions.title: Select a licensed, legally accessible market-data source for opening/closing lines; store odds with provenance like every other source. Nothing in this module can grade CLV (V-03) or measure correlation (C-01–C-05) until this is decided.
suggestions.problem: Unblocks the primary skill-vs-luck mechanism of the whole leaderboard.
suggestions.evidence: NFL integrity & betting policy (no official odds source exists)
options: Review the linked official evidence and decide before implementation.
suggestions.recommendation: Proposed in the already merged NFL Lines module; this is not an approval to implement.
suggestions.decision_needed: OWNER DECISION (Q2): provider, jurisdiction/legal review, budget.

suggestions.title: Publish an explicit risk policy for any real-world use: bankroll unit definition, max exposure per game/day, parlay-leg cap, and a hard rule that no strategy is 'live' until gates V1–V8 pass.
suggestions.problem: Removes the largest decision-risk: acting on unvalidated strategies.
suggestions.evidence: NFL integrity & betting policy
options: Review the linked official evidence and decide before implementation.
suggestions.recommendation: Proposed in the already merged NFL Lines module; this is not an approval to implement.
suggestions.decision_needed: OWNER DECISION (Q1/Q6): values and enforcement point.

suggestions.title: Category landing page that mirrors how decisions are actually made
suggestions.problem: The site is organised by data source (NFL, MLB, radio) rather than by the decisions it supports, so a reviewer has to know where to look before they can decide anything.
suggestions.evidence: Current navigation lists fifteen parallel pages; the NFL Lines pages added in this session would make twenty-two with no entry point that groups them by decision type.
options: A. Add a decision-based landing page that links to every table and states what each table can and cannot answer.
B. Leave the navigation as-is and add a single 'NFL Lines' dropdown.
C. Rebuild the whole site around decisions (rejected: it breaks the existing source-linked pages and the audit trail).
suggestions.recommendation: Option A. Build a decision-first landing page that links every table, states the verification label of that table and names the question it answers.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm the decision categories to be used as the landing page headings.

suggestions.title: Show the verification label and the capture timestamp on every table row, not only in the source column
suggestions.problem: A reader can currently see that a row has a source link but not how fresh the source is, so a week-old injury designation looks as current as this morning's.
suggestions.evidence: The official NFL injury report page is republished each week, and the official team depth charts carry their own 'updated as of' date; the 49ers chart captured in this session is dated 11/10/26 while the Miami and Baltimore charts publish no date at all.
options: A. Add a 'verified on' column plus the source's own as-of date to every table.
B. Add a page-level snapshot banner only (current behaviour, weaker).
C. Colour-code rows by age (rejected: colour alone fails accessibility and hides the value).
suggestions.recommendation: Option A, with the source's own as-of date shown separately from the capture timestamp so a chart that publishes no date is visibly undated rather than falsely fresh.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm whether rows without a source as-of date should be hidden from the default view or shown with an UNDATED badge.

suggestions.title: Model transparency panel on every originated line
suggestions.problem: A fair line is only actionable if the reader can see its inputs, their official sources and the sensitivity of the number to each assumption.
suggestions.evidence: The originated lines depend on a Pythagorean exponent, an assumed margin standard deviation, a home-edge assumption, a rest coefficient and an availability penalty table; the published line moves when any of them moves.
options: A. Expandable inputs panel per line with the sensitivity of the line to each parameter.
B. A single methodology page (current behaviour).
C. Publish only the final number (rejected: it hides the assumptions that the gates are supposed to police).
suggestions.recommendation: Option A, including a sensitivity line such as 'line moves to X if the margin standard deviation is 10 instead of 12'.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm which parameters must be exposed and whether the sensitivity view is a table or a chart.

suggestions.title: Gate status as a visible column on every strategy and line row
suggestions.problem: A strategy that cannot yet be judged looks identical to one that has been judged and failed, which is how unvalidated ideas quietly get treated as validated ones.
suggestions.evidence: The ten strategy records have gate results including PASS, PARTIAL and NOT TESTABLE states. The leaderboard remains gated until price and settlement evidence exists.
options: A. Add a gate badge column with a hover explanation of the blocking gate.
B. Keep gates on a separate page only.
C. Hide strategies that are not eligible (rejected: it hides the work and the reasons).
suggestions.recommendation: Option A, and treat NOT TESTABLE as its own badge rather than as a pass or a fail.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm the badge wording for a strategy that is blocked only by missing data.

suggestions.title: Capture all 32 official team depth charts on a schedule instead of by hand
suggestions.problem: Depth coverage is the single largest gap in the tracker: three clubs have a captured chart, so for the other 29 clubs the tier of every injured player is unknown and no availability penalty can be computed.
suggestions.evidence: Depth captures exist for three clubs only. The other 29 are unverified. No automated depth-capture script exists in this branch.
options: A. Run the capture on a scheduled job and publish the manifest with SHA-256 for each chart.
B. Keep manual capture (rejected: it does not scale and does not keep history).
C. Use a third-party depth aggregator (rejected: not an official source).
suggestions.recommendation: Option A, and store two dated captures per club per week so the tier diff required by strategy S-09 becomes computable.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm the capture frequency (weekly is the minimum that supports the tier diff).

suggestions.title: Official automation for every NFL Lines source
suggestions.problem: The sources used by this program are fetched with the platform fetch tool during a session, so the capture is not reproducible and cannot be re-run on a schedule.
suggestions.evidence: The existing repository already solves this for the free-time dashboard with scripts/fetch_official.py and a GitHub Actions workflow; this program needs the same pattern for injury reports, depth charts, standings and schedules.
options: A. Add scripts/fetch_nfl_lines.py with a SHA-256 manifest and a scheduled workflow, mirroring the existing pattern.
B. Rely on manual capture.
C. Fetch from the visitor's browser (rejected).
suggestions.recommendation: Option A. A reproducible NFL-specific fetcher and scheduled workflow do not yet exist in this branch; implement them before calling these captures automated or re-runnable.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm whether a scheduled workflow may be enabled by default or only on request.

suggestions.title: A price source, or an explicit decision to run the program without one
suggestions.problem: Edge, ROI and leaderboard points cannot be computed without a price, and no official source publishes NFL betting lines, so the program currently originates fair values only.
suggestions.evidence: The NFL publishes schedules, results, injury reports and standings on nfl.com; none of the official pages carries a price. Every gate that scores a strategy (G2, G5, G9, G12) is blocked on this.
options: A. Connect the program's own bet log, in which the owner records the price and timestamp of every bet taken.
B. Connect a licensed price feed.
C. Run the program as a pure line-origination and analysis system with no scoring.
D. Infer prices from third-party pages (rejected: not an official source and not reproducible).
suggestions.recommendation: Option A or C. A is strictly better because it makes every gate testable with the owner's own records; C is the honest fallback if no bet log exists.
suggestions.effort: Low for A, High for B
suggestions.decision_needed: Choose between A, B and C. This single choice unlocks or permanently blocks the scoring half of the program.

suggestions.title: Historical injury panel so the availability strategies can be back-tested
suggestions.problem: Only one week of official injury data has been captured, so the availability strategies cannot be measured against any outcome.
suggestions.evidence: The NFL publishes an official injury report for every week of the season at /injuries/league/<season>/<week>, and each week can be captured as a dated snapshot.
options: A. Capture weeks 1 to 10 of the 2026 season as dated snapshots (10 captures) and pair them with the official final scores already captured.
B. Capture two more weeks as a pilot.
C. Skip and rely on the schedule panel only.
suggestions.recommendation: Option A, but ten injury reports do not automatically provide 100 settled, priced bets; the price and settlement requirements must also be met.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm how many weeks to capture this season and whether to keep the raw weekly snapshots permanently.

suggestions.title: Publish the luck baseline next to every measured statistic
suggestions.problem: A measured effect is meaningless without its noise floor, and the available historical panel shows limited season-to-season persistence while the game-level model leaves substantial margin variance unexplained.
suggestions.evidence: On the official 2024–2025 completed-season standings panel (32 team pairs), points differential per game has year-to-year r = 0.32, r² = 0.10. Separately, the exploratory game-level model leaves 79.5% of margin variance unexplained. Neither statistic is a causal partition of betting skill versus luck.
options: A. Publish the baseline statistic beside every effect size and require the effect to exceed it.
B. Keep the baseline on a separate analysis page.
C. Skip the baseline (rejected: it is the difference between a strategy and a coin flip).
suggestions.recommendation: Option A. Every published effect should carry the number it has to beat, in the same row.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm whether the luck baseline should be shown as a percentage or as a required margin.

suggestions.title: Require a declared hypothesis and a registered gate set before a strategy can be listed
suggestions.problem: A catalogue that grows by adding ideas will eventually contain strategies that were designed after seeing the results, which is how a backtest becomes a fit.
options: A. Registration form: hypothesis, official inputs, gates and the date registered, all published with the strategy.
B. Keep the catalogue informal.
C. Allow retrospective registration with a note.
suggestions.recommendation: Option A, with the registration date visible on the leaderboard so a late registration is obvious.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm who registers a strategy and who reviews registrations.

suggestions.title: Add a live leaderboard page rendering per-division standings from a graded-selections JSON once the grading pipeline exists; every row links to the official result sources used.
suggestions.problem: Makes the competition auditable and reward-eligible statuses visible.
suggestions.evidence: NFL Big Data Bowl (official precedent)
options: Review the linked official evidence and decide before implementation.
suggestions.recommendation: Proposed in the already merged NFL Lines module; this is not an approval to implement.
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve scoring formula weights (B-03/B-04) before implementation.

suggestions.title: Add CSV/JSON export buttons to every table (data rows already carry structured source URLs).
suggestions.problem: Lets reviewers analyze rows offline and keeps sessions from re-scraping.
suggestions.evidence: Repo official event JSON (existing structured data)
options: Review the linked official evidence and decide before implementation.
suggestions.recommendation: Proposed in the already merged NFL Lines module; this is not an approval to implement.
suggestions.decision_needed: Low-risk; approve and implement in a build pass.

suggestions.title: Per-club pages: next game, availability snapshot, recent transactions, roster ACT changes, and our model's own number when one exists.
suggestions.problem: Turns the module from league-wide tables into decision-ready team views.
suggestions.evidence: NFL.com roster pages
options: Review the linked official evidence and decide before implementation.
suggestions.recommendation: Proposed in the already merged NFL Lines module; this is not an approval to implement.
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve page template; data feeds exist or are proposed above.

suggestions.title: Give the Suggestions page an explicit owner-review loop: each suggestion gets a decision record (decided/approved/rejected + date) appended to COORDINATION.md before any implementation begins.
suggestions.problem: Satisfies the requirement that suggestions are reviewed before changes, and keeps parallel sessions coordinated.
suggestions.evidence: COORDINATION.md (shared task board)
options: Review the linked official evidence and decide before implementation.
suggestions.recommendation: Proposed in the already merged NFL Lines module; this is not an approval to implement.
suggestions.decision_needed: OWNER DECISION (Q10): who reviews and approves.

suggestions.title: Evidence drawer that shows the exact official excerpt behind each value
suggestions.problem: A source link proves where a value came from but not what the official page actually said, so a reviewer still has to open the page and search for the row.
suggestions.evidence: Official team depth-chart pages are the primary sources, but source excerpts are not currently stored alongside each parsed value. The evidence-drawer proposal is therefore a new provenance feature, not a feature already supported by saved excerpts.
options: A. Store a short quoted excerpt with each parsed row and show it inline on hover and in a detail panel.
B. Keep only the link (current behaviour).
C. Re-fetch pages live from the visitor's browser (rejected: it leaks the visitor's IP to many hosts and breaks the offline audit).
suggestions.recommendation: Option A. Store the excerpt, its source URL and the capture timestamp together so each cell can be audited without leaving the page.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm the maximum excerpt length and whether excerpts are stored for every row or only for rows that carry a modelled value.

suggestions.title: Filter presets for the two questions people actually ask: 'what is unavailable' and 'where is the line thin'
suggestions.problem: The tables are searchable but not preset for the two operational questions, so a reviewer must build filters by hand for every team.
suggestions.evidence: The official Week 10 report snapshot contains 298 rows across all 32 clubs, including league-reported no-injury rows; the actual designated-out count should be calculated from the designations, not guessed.
options: A. Ship saved filters: designated-out only, defence only, starters only, unverified-depth only.
B. Add a faceted filter panel (position, unit, designation, depth tier).
C. Both (A first, B when the data set is complete).
suggestions.recommendation: Option C. Ship A immediately because the data supports it today, and specify B so the panel can be added once all 32 clubs have a captured depth chart.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm which presets are wanted first.

suggestions.title: Side-by-side comparison of two clubs' availability
suggestions.problem: A bet on one side of a game needs both clubs' depth position side by side, and the current single-table view forces the reviewer to hold two rows in their head.
suggestions.evidence: The deficiency model already produces one row per team per game, so the comparison is a presentation change rather than a data change.
options: A. Per-game card with both clubs, the depth tiers and the resulting penalty.
B. A comparison table with one row per game and columns for each club.
C. Downloadable CSV only (rejected: it does not help review).
suggestions.recommendation: Option B as the default view with A as the detail view for a single game.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm whether the comparison view should include the next week's games as well as the current week.

suggestions.title: Official per-player usage data for the player-prop strategies
suggestions.problem: Two of the ten strategies are player-prop strategies and neither can produce a number, because the program has no official per-player usage history.
suggestions.evidence: The two registered player-prop strategies lack a historical official player-usage panel in this repository. This proposal is about collecting that missing input; no specific replacement-quarterback cases are asserted here.
options: A. Capture official per-player season and game logs and compute usage shares.
B. Express the prop strategies as exclusions only: refuse to take a prop on a player whose tier moved down.
C. Use projection sites (rejected: not official and not reproducible).
suggestions.recommendation: Option B immediately, because it is computable from the depth data already captured, with A as the follow-up that allows priced props.
suggestions.effort: Medium for A, Low for B
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm whether priced props are wanted at all, or whether prop coverage should stay exclusion-only.

suggestions.title: Weekly review workflow that closes the loop from flag to fix
suggestions.problem: The site publishes irregularities for review, but nothing tracks whether a flagged item was reviewed, and this repository already shows that review records can be lost between sessions.
suggestions.evidence: The coordination log of this repository records past irregularities (IR-018 to IR-021) and the fact that earlier review sessions had to re-derive their corrections independently.
options: A. Every flag carries a status (open, reviewed, corrected, accepted) and a dated review note.
B. Flags stay read-only.
C. Move flags into the suggestions register (rejected: a flag is a defect, a suggestion is an improvement).
suggestions.recommendation: Option A, with the same status vocabulary as the suggestions register.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm the flag status vocabulary and who is allowed to close a flag.

suggestions.title: Publish the derived tables as downloadable data next to the pages
suggestions.problem: A reviewer who wants to recompute a statistic has to scrape the table, which makes the published numbers hard to reproduce independently.
suggestions.evidence: Every derived table in this program is already written to a JSON file under data/nfl/, and the existing dashboard already publishes its raw event JSON.
options: A. Publish the JSON for each new page with a link on the page.
B. Publish CSV only.
C. Keep the data private (rejected: it defeats the verification model).
suggestions.recommendation: Option A, matching the existing dashboard convention, so a reviewer can recompute the published correlations.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm whether CSV exports are needed in addition to JSON.

suggestions.title: Record the league's own rule-based context for the strategies that depend on it
suggestions.problem: Several candidate signals are rule-driven (the injury report filing deadlines, the designation rules, the roster cutdown rules that decide who is available), and none of that context is currently on the site.
suggestions.evidence: The official NFL important-dates page states the weekly practice-report and game-status-report filing deadlines that determine when an official designation exists at all.
options: A. Add an official-context table that links the rule to the strategies it constrains.
B. Leave the rules in the methodology text only.
suggestions.recommendation: Option A. It explains why a designation can be missing rather than being negative, which is the most common misreading of the injury table.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm whether the rule context belongs on the strategy pages or on a single rules page.

suggestions.title: Publish a per-source freshness dashboard
suggestions.problem: The program reads from sources with very different refresh cycles (weekly injury reports, dated depth charts, season standings, and a schedule that changes on official notice) and the reader cannot see which are stale.
suggestions.evidence: In this session the official standings page was current to the day, the 49ers depth chart was dated 11/10/26, the Miami and Baltimore charts publish no date at all, and the schedule snapshots are dated 2026-11-02.
options: A. One table listing every source, its owner, its refresh cycle and the age of the last capture.
B. Put the age next to each table (part of SG-02).
C. Rely on the capture timestamps already shown.
suggestions.recommendation: Option A as the single place to see the whole program's freshness, reusing the SG-02 row badge for detail.
suggestions.decision_needed: Confirm whether the refresh cycle for each source should be declared by the program or read from the source itself.

priority_note: Suggested priority is a review aid only, not an accepted implementation plan. P1 means likely to unblock evidence or prevent misleading decisions; P2 means useful after the P1 evidence foundations. Reviewers may change it before implementation.
